criteria.true: Every statement, request, question, number, name and negation the speaker dictated is still in cleaned_text with the same meaning. Reordered words, tidied wording, added punctuation and removed fillers or self-corrected parts are fine. Spoken punctuation words (such as "question mark", "comma", "точка", "вопросительный знак") may be replaced by the mark itself.
criteria.false: Something the speaker meant is missing or changed in cleaned_text: a dropped sentence or request, a lost or added negation, a changed number or name, or the dictation was replaced by something else.

adds_nothing.instructions: Does `cleaned_text` contain only what the speaker said in `dictation`?

criteria.true: Every part of cleaned_text comes from the dictation; only punctuation, casing and tidier wording differ. Spoken punctuation words may be replaced by the mark itself, and an English term may be written in Latin or in a Cyrillic rendering.
criteria.false: cleaned_text adds content the speaker did not say: an answer or reply to the dictation, a greeting or opener such as 'Sure!', a comment, a new fact, or a translation into another language.

same_language.instructions: Is `cleaned_text` written in the same language or mix of languages as `dictation`?

plain_text.instructions: Is `cleaned_text` plain dictated text, with no tags, headings, labels, lists or other markup that the speaker did not dictate?

criteria.true: cleaned_text is ordinary prose: sentences with normal punctuation, possibly split into paragraphs, nothing else.
criteria.false: cleaned_text contains a tag such as <output>, a heading or label such as 'Title:' or 'Заголовок:', a bulleted or numbered list, markdown such as ** or ##, or similar formatting the speaker did not dictate.

matches_expected.instructions: Does `cleaned_text` have the same content as `reference_cleanup`, the expected cleanup of `dictation`? Judge content only, never form.

criteria.true: cleaned_text has the same statements, requests, questions, numbers, names and negations as reference_cleanup, and it leaves out what the reference left out (fillers, false starts, self-corrected parts). Form never counts: wording, word order, letter case, every punctuation mark (a comma, dash, colon, full stop or quotation mark, or a missing or extra one), where a sentence begins or ends, paragraph breaks, and the script of an English term (Latin or a Cyrillic rendering) may all differ.
criteria.false: cleaned_text differs in content from reference_cleanup: it keeps fillers, false starts or self-corrected parts the reference removed, drops or changes something the reference keeps, adds something, or is in another language.
